title: Bidirectional BFS in Valencia: Meet-in-the-Middle!
description: Watch Bidirectional BFS split the journey from start and goal at the same time, dramatically shrinking the search space. This pathfinding visualization maps the idea onto real street-like graphs where connectivity, layers, and fronts collide.
ig_caption:
🌍🚦 Valencia’s El Cabanyal street grid turns into a graph where every intersection is a node and every road segment is an edge. With **Bidirectional BFS**, we run BFS from both the **start** and the **goal** simultaneously—two expanding frontiers that “meet in the middle,” cutting the exploration from roughly **O(b^d)** down toward **O(b^(d/2))** when branching factors are similar. 🤝

📌 In graph-theory terms: undirected (or symmetrically traversable) graphs, shortest-path guarantee via layered expansion, and termination the moment the two search trees touch. Because real maps have irregular connectivity, this often beats one-sided BFS by avoiding vast regions that are clearly irrelevant once fronts converge. 🔍🗺️

👉 Want to see how the frontier layers evolve frame-by-frame? Like, follow, and comment **“FRONTIER”**—I’ll generate the next visualization with different start/goal points!
fb_caption:
🚦 In this pathfinding visualization from Valencia (El Cabanyal), we use **Bidirectional BFS** to search a street-like graph from both ends. Instead of expanding outward from only the start (slow for long distances), two BFS frontiers grow until they meet, preserving the shortest-path guarantee while reducing unnecessary exploration.

🧠 Learn the graph-search mechanics, then share this with a friend who loves algorithms—comment your favorite BFS trick!
yt_description:
Bidirectional BFS visualization in Valencia (El Cabanyal)! 🚦🌍

In this YouTube Shorts, we show how **Bidirectional BFS** finds the shortest path by launching two BFS searches—one from the start node and one from the goal node—then stopping as soon as the frontiers intersect. Perfect for learning graph theory, frontier expansion layers, and why meet-in-the-middle dramatically reduces search work on real street-map style graphs.

Keywords: bidirectional bfs, pathfinding, shortest path, graph search, computerscience, algorithm visualization, BFS, real map graph.

Watch to the end 👀 and comment what next city/terrain you want!
